findings.summary: The prefix rule contradicts the minimal example's behaviour: the minimal router uses route '/' under '/items', which the page elsewhere implies gives '/items/', but page 5 says '/items' redirects.
findings.evidence: Prefix | Route path | Final URL ... /items | / | /items/ ... Route / under a prefix: /items redirects to /items/
findings.fix: Add one line on page 1 noting that a request to /items redirects to /items/, so learners see the same rule on both pages.

findings.summary: The text says to call include_router once per router, but the next bullet and the example mount the same router twice.
findings.evidence: "app.include_router(router) registers all its routes; call it once per router" vs. "So one router mounts under /v1 and /v2 without edits" and the example calling app.include_router(users.router, prefix="/v1") then prefix="/v2".
findings.fix: Reword to "call it once per mount" or "once for each place the router is mounted".

findings.summary: Bullet holds two ideas: router-level dependency return values are discarded, and what to use them for.
findings.evidence: Router-level dependencies=[Depends(verify_token)] return values are discarded
findings.fix: Split it into two bullets: 'Return values of router-level dependencies are discarded' and 'Use them for auth checks and side effects only'. Put the example in the table row for dependencies.

findings.summary: Code for mounting the same router twice is shown before the idea behind it is stated.
findings.evidence: app.include_router(router) registers all its routes; call it once per router ... So one router mounts under /v1 and /v2 without edits
findings.fix: State the idea first ('Same router can mount under many prefixes') and then show the code. Also fix the contradiction between 'call it once per router' and the two-mount example, for instance by saying 'once per mount'.

findings.summary: The nesting process is shown as fragmented labels, so the path build-up is hard to follow.
findings.evidence:
child route
/users
parent.include_router(child, prefix='/admin')
/admin/users
app.include_router(parent, prefix='/api/v1')
/api/v1/admin/users
findings.fix: Show it as a small table or a chain with one row per step: route /users → child in parent with /admin → /admin/users → parent in app with /api/v1 → /api/v1/admin/users.

findings.summary: Code is shown before its one-line idea, and a bullet holds two ideas.
findings.evidence:
Schemas = API contract; models = DB tables
Services are plain functions: testable without HTTP, reusable from CLI or jobs
findings.fix: Split each into separate bullets (schemas = API contract / models = DB tables; testable without HTTP / reusable from CLI or jobs). Put the from_attributes idea before the UserRead snippet.

findings.summary: Bullets pack several ideas, such as precedence order, case-insensitivity and coercion.
findings.evidence: Env vars override .env, which overrides field defaults; names are case-insensitive
findings.fix: Split into 'Priority: env vars > .env > defaults' and 'Env names are case-insensitive'. The priority diagram on the same page already covers the first, so drop the duplicated text there.

findings.summary: Priority is stated as prose and as a diagram on the same page, and the page shows both a module global and a cached getter without saying which to choose.
findings.evidence:
Module global | settings = Settings() in app/core/config.py | import it everywhere
Cached getter | @lru_cache def get_settings() | read .env once, inject it
findings.fix: Add a clear recommendation, for example 'Default to the cached getter, since tests can override it with dependency_overrides'. Page 6 says 'settings = Settings()  # or @lru_cache get_settings' without saying which is preferred.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "instantiating", "forgetting").
findings.evidence: Mistakes: instantiating the app in a module other modules import from (import app from main), forgetting prefix leading slash, route '/' with trailing-slash redirect surprises, putting business logic in routers, calling Settings() in many places
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The mistakes list has bullets that each hold a problem and a fix, and the import cycle diagram is shown as arrows in text.
findings.evidence: Route / under a prefix: /items redirects to /items/
findings.fix: Turn the mistakes list into a Mistake | Fix table. Draw the cycle as a two-node diagram. Also resolve the 'Route / under a prefix' bullet against page 1, which recommends a '/' route under /items.
